title: HTTP and Response Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain what http and response performance contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: response caching.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. In this lesson, focus on response caching; then compare it with compression. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use http and response performance when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
